## Summary

I implemented support for typed/cast literals inside SQL `ARRAY[...]` constructors in the `polars-sql` crate. All changes are in source files (`crates/polars-sql/src/`); nothing under `tests/` was touched.

### Changes

**`crates/polars-sql/src/types.rs`**
- Made `timeunit_from_precision` `pub(crate)` so the typed-literal handler can reuse the same precision→`TimeUnit` mapping as `map_sql_dtype_to_polars`.

**`crates/polars-sql/src/sql_expr.rs`**
1. **`array_expr_to_series`** — array elements can now be `SQLExpr::TypedString` (`DATE '…'`, `TIME '…'`, `TIMESTAMP(n) '…'`) and `SQLExpr::Cast` (both `'…'::type` and `CAST('…' AS type)`). Each such element is turned into an `Expr` via `visit_expr` and evaluated to a scalar `AnyValue` (new helper `eval_expr_to_any_value`). Nested arrays recurse, so `ARRAY[['42'::int16], …]` → `List(List(Int16))`.
2. Added an explicit **dtype-consistency check** before building the series: mixing incompatible element types (e.g. `DATE` + `TIME`) raises a `SQLInterface` error whose message contains `expected consistent dtypes` (surfaced as `SQLInterfaceError` in Python).
3. **`TypedString` `TIMESTAMP`/`DATETIME` handler** now binds the precision and passes the correct time unit to `to_datetime`, so `TIMESTAMP(3) '…'` yields `Datetime('ms')` (previously only precision-less `TIMESTAMP`/`DATETIME` was accepted).
4. **`visit_cast`** now routes a string-literal cast to `Time` (e.g. `'01:02:03'::time`) through `.str().to_time(...)`, because the standard cast kernels don't support `String → Time` (Date/Datetime/numeric casts already work and are unchanged).

### Verification
I built a scratch example driving `SQLContext` end-to-end (removed afterward) and confirmed every required case produces the exact type and values:
- `List(Date)`, `List(Time)`, `List(Datetime('ms'))` for temporal typed literals
- `List(Date/Time/Int64/Float64)` for `::` casts, `List(Date)` for `CAST(... AS DATE)`
- `List(List(Int16))` and `List(List(Date))` for nested arrays
- The `DATE`/`TIME` mix errors with `...expected consistent dtypes (found date and time)`
- Existing `[10,20,30]` / `['a','b','c']` bracket literals still work
